summary: At aerodromes you observe other traffic, conform with the circuit, turn left unless told otherwise, and land and take off into wind. You may not land on an occupied runway without ATC authority. During notified watch hours you may not operate in an ATZ without permission (ATC) or information (AFIS/AGCS), and you must report position and height entering and leaving. Joining aircraft give way to traffic in the circuit. Built from the Skyway Code pp.96-99.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), pp.96-99
sections: Operating rules (SERA.3225)
Observe other traffic to avoid collision, conform with or avoid the circuit pattern
All turns to the left when approaching to land or take off unless otherwise indicated
Land and take off into wind unless safety dictates otherwise
On landing, leave clear to your left any other aircraft landing or about to take off, and move clear of the landing area as soon as possible
When taking up position for take-off leave clear on your left any aircraft that has taken off or is about to
ATZ rules (Rule 11 and 12)
Rule 10: do not land on a runway occupied by another aircraft unless authorised by ATC
Rule 11: during notified hours of ATC, AFIS or AGCS, do not operate within an ATZ unless you have permission (ATC) or have obtained information (AFIS or AGCS)
Keep a continuous watch on the frequency or for visual signals and transmit position and height on entering or leaving the ATZ
Rule 12: do not taxi on the manoeuvring area of an uncontrolled aerodrome without the permission of the person in charge or the AFIS unit
The circuit
Legs: crosswind, downwind, base, final, with the liveside and deadside
Standard radio calls at downwind and final. Also announce base or late downwind if it helps situational awareness
Joining aircraft give way to traffic already established
Always make position calls even if you know of no other traffic, with blind calls if no AGCS or AFIS. Non-radio aircraft are a possibility
If in doubt on local procedure, ask by phone or radio. AFIS and AGCS will not give instructions to airborne aircraft
Departure procedures
Obtain runway in use, circuit direction and QNH or QFE before taxiing. Larger aerodromes provide ATIS: quote the information letter

At a controlled aerodrome request permission to taxi. At an AGCS aerodrome no taxi clearance is needed but you must have the permission of the person in charge. At an AFIS aerodrome request taxi instructions
Complete power and pre-take-off checks at the holding point before saying 'ready for departure'
At an AFIS aerodrome the service reverts to information only: the pilot ensures it is safe to enter the runway
At an ATC aerodrome you must not enter the runway without clearance (take-off clearance or 'line up and wait')
Stop at an angle at the holding point for a good view of the approach, particularly in a high-wing aircraft
Report leaving the ATZ. At large aerodromes, moving-map aerodrome charts are helpful. Hot spots are circled in red on charts

sum.Operating rules (SERA.3225): Left turns, into wind and leave clear to the left.
sum.ATZ rules (Rule 11 and 12): Permission or information in the ATZ, and taxiing rules.
sum.The circuit: Legs, calls and giving way when joining.
sum.Departure procedures: Runway in use, taxi, hold, ready and report leaving the ATZ.

cards.q: Which way do you turn in the circuit unless told otherwise?
Which direction do you land and take off?
cards.a: Into wind unless safety dictates otherwise.

cards.q: What does Rule 10 say about runways?
cards.a: Do not land on an occupied runway unless authorised by ATC.
Operating within an ATZ during notified hours of watch.
Taxiing on the manoeuvring area of an uncontrolled aerodrome.

cards.q: Do you need a taxi clearance at an AGCS aerodrome?
cards.a: No, but you need the permission of the person in charge.

cards.q: What do you request at an AFIS aerodrome before taxiing?
Who must you give way to when joining the circuit?
What must be transmitted on entering or leaving an ATZ?
What are hot spots on aerodrome charts?
cards.a: Holding points vulnerable to runway incursion, circled in red.

cards.q: Which clearance allows runway entry at an ATC aerodrome?
cards.a: Take-off clearance or 'line up and wait'.

cards.q: What must you call after departing the ATZ?

quiz.q: Unless told otherwise, circuit turns are:
o: Right
Left
Either
Depends on wind
quiz.why: All turns left when approaching to land or take off unless indicated.

quiz.q: At an AFIS aerodrome, when you report 'ready for departure':
o: The service reverts to information only and you ensure it is safe
You receive a take-off clearance from the AFIS officer
ATC separates you from other traffic in the circuit
You must hold until the AFIS officer clears you to go
quiz.why: AFIS gives information, not clearances, once you are at the holding point.

quiz.q: Rule 11 requires, in an ATZ with an AGCS, that you:
o: Obtain appropriate information
Get permission from the AGCS operator
Hold off until called by the operator
Squawk 7700 and call on entry
quiz.why: For AFIS or AGCS you get information, with ATC you get permission.

o: Give way to traffic already in the circuit
Have priority over traffic in the circuit
Join on final ahead of circuit traffic
Squawk ident and wait for a clearance
quiz.why: Joining aircraft give way to established traffic.

quiz.q: Before taxiing at an aerodrome with ATIS, you should quote:
o: The information letter on first contact
The QFE you have set, on first contact
The squawk you are using, on first contact
Your fuel on board, on first contact
quiz.why: Give the ATIS letter on first contact with ATC.
